Home
French School Abroad
Jeannine Manuel School is a co-educational bilingual international school for 3-18 year olds in the heart of London, welcoming students with all levels of French.
& Care

Mission & Vision
Our Vision
Jeannine Manuel founded the Ecole Active Bilingue in 1954 with the mission to develop international understanding through bilingual education starting in the nursery years. Her premise was that “learning a foreign language is, by itself, important; it is also a means to better understand others, to be able to think like them - it provides access to the world.”
In France, since its founding, over seventy years ago, École Jeannine Manuel has become the largest non-denominational independent school in France, with 3,250 students in Paris and Lille representing over eighty nationalities.
Today, all over the world, wherever they live, study or work, twenty thousand alumni bear witness to the excellence of the education they received, as well as to a spirit of openness and flexibility forged at École Jeannine Manuel.
Our Mission
Our school’s mission is to promote international understanding through the bilingual education of a multicultural community of students, and to foster pedagogical innovation by exploring best practices in an ever-changing global environment.
...our pedagogical principles

About Us
Jeannine Manuel founded the Ecole Active Bilingue in Paris in 1954 with the mission to develop international understanding through outstanding bilingual education starting in the nursery years. Her premise was that “learning a foreign language is, by itself, important; it is also a means to better understand others, to be able to think like them - it provides access to the world.”
With a rich history spanning several decades and countries, the network of Jeannine Manuel Schools share a same commitment to their founders' mission: to promote international understanding through the bilingual education of a multicultural community of students, and to foster pedagogical innovation by exploring best practices in an ever-changing global environment.
...our mission & vision
...our sister Schools

Accreditations & Policies
Jeannine Manuel School is uniquely positioned at the crossroads of several educational systems, including British and French. Our accreditations reflect this distinctive identity as well as our commitment to academic excellence and international understanding, all while following rigorous international standards.
This accreditation framework allows our students to pursue world-class qualifications that open doors to top universities across the UK, France, the US, and beyond.
Jeannine Manuel School is accredited by the Independent Schools Association (ISA), the leading association of British independent schools. This accreditation means that our school is inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), the inspectorate appointed by the Department for Education (DfE) to inspect private schools in the UK. ISI follow the same DfE-issued regulations as Ofsted when inspecting schools.

Contact Information
If you have concerns about any pupil at Jeannine Manuel School, please contact the Safeguarding Team: dsl@jmanuel.uk or 0203 829 5970.
Our DSL is Peter Cogavin. Our Deputy DSLs are Pauline Prévot, Severine Liger-Galopin, Jeanne Gonnet, Lorna France, Agathe Brillet, Louise Matharan-Brizard and Henrietta Knight.
If you think a child is in immediate danger, do not delay: call 999.
Further information can be found in our Safeguarding Policy.
Jeannine Manuel School is exempt from the Learning & Development requirements of the Statutory Framework for EYFS. This is because our pupils first learn to read and write in French, which conflicts with the EYFS literacy goals. Jeannine Manuel School continues to uphold high expectations for all the pupils working within the EYFS framework. The safeguarding and welfare requirements of the EYFS still apply.

History
After joining the French Resistance and becoming a member of the London Free French in 1940, Jeannine Manuel returned to France for the Liberation of Paris in August 1944. She returned firmly convinced that ignorance breeds fear and that fear is the root cause of human conflict. Scroll down to find out more about our school’s fascinating history and Jeannine Manuel’s extraordinary vision.
1954: Founding of École Active Bilingue
Jeannine Manuel founded the École Active Bilingue (now École Jeannine Manuel) in Paris with the mission to promote international understanding through bilingual education, starting from the nursery years. Her belief was that learning a foreign language not only helps to understand others but also opens access to the world.
For Jeannine Manuel, the aim of education is to help shape ‘whole’ people, individuals aware of their presence in this world, engaged in its history, and ready to play a part in world affairs.
From 9 students enrolled in September to 100 by January, the school rapidly continued to expand: over the next decades, École Jeannine Manuel became the largest non-denominational independent school in France, serving over 3,250 students from more than 80 nationalities at present.
1979: A Landmark Opening at Rue du Théâtre
In 1979, Jeannine Manuel opened a new school at 70 Rue du Théâtre in Paris’ 15th arrondissement—an address that soon became synonymous with the school’s outstanding bilingual education. It welcomed a community of families and teachers drawn to its spirit of innovation, and more than four decades on, remains a vibrant embodiment of Jeannine Manuel’s educational vision.
1992: Opening of Lille Campus
In 1992, the school further expanded with the opening of a new campus in Marcq-en-Barœul, a few kilometers from Lille. Its boarding school welcomes international students from all over the world.
2014: The school celebrates its 60th birthday and is renamed École Jeannine Manuel
On the occasion of its sixtieth birthday, the school was officially renamed École Jeannine Manuel and underwent a visual rebrand. A new logo was designed and the school chose a new motto that perfectly encapsulates Jeannine Manuel’s original vision for the school: “International understanding through a bilingual education”.
2015: Ecole Jeannine Manuel opens in London
In 2015, with the financial support of the Fondation Jeannine Manuel and in honour of Jeannine Manuel’s formative years in London, the school opened its first site in Bedford Square, London.
2019: Expansion to Russell Square
In 2019, in response to the steady growth of our student body, our school expanded beyond its historic Bedford Square home to open a dedicated Upper School building at 52-53 Russell Square. Just a few minutes’ walk away, this beautifully restored site offers state-of-the-art facilities, including laboratories, a comprehensive library, and inviting common rooms designed for independent study and collaboration.
Our Upper School provides a university-style environment that fosters academic focus, autonomy, and maturity, while preserving the warm, caring community that defines our school. This dedicated space empowers students to thrive, both in their final years and beyond.
2022: A New Primary School Building
In 2022, our growing Primary School moved into a newly renovated Georgian building designed to meet the needs of an expanding community. The new building features three dedicated spacious outdoor play areas, allowing children to move, explore and grow through active learning. Two multi-purpose halls and a climbing wall serve the entire school community, bringing students of all ages together for assemblies, sport, performances and celebrations.
2024: Ecole Jeannine Manuel in London becomes Jeannine Manuel School
In September 2024, having grown from an initial population of 185 students to 700 and expanded to three sites across Bloomsbury, École Jeannine Manuel in London became Jeannine Manuel School, reflecting its position in the London's landscape of top British and international schools while remaining true to its roots and identity as one of three Jeannine Manuel schools.

Our Parents' Association
Through its different projects and initiatives, our incredible Parents' Association brings the school’s mission to life all year round and is a crucial part of our community.
What does the Parents' Association do?
Our families are at the heart of our community, and the Jeannine Manuel Parents’ Association plays a vital role in bringing everyone together while supporting school life in countless meaningful ways.
Open to all families, the Parents’ Association organises a rich calendar of events and initiatives - from Friday morning coffees and welcome picnics to cultural celebrations, educational outings, and the much-loved Family Funday. These moments help create lasting memories for students and parents alike.
Beyond events, our Parents’ Association serves as a welcoming hub for new families and a valuable point of connection for parents with questions, ideas, or a desire to get involved.
Thank you, Jeannine Manuel Parents’ Association, for everything you do to help our school community!
For more information latest news, upcoming events, and more, consult the JMPA website (password protected)

Our Team
At Jeannine Manuel School, our leadership team brings together deep educational expertise, a shared commitment to innovation, and a steadfast belief in the school’s mission. Guided by our motto - Think, Dare, Share & Care - our Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees work collaboratively to ensure academic excellence, student wellbeing, and the continuous evolution of our bilingual, international approach. Together, they shape a learning environment where every student can thrive, and where our values are brought to life every day.

Sister Schools
A Shared Vision Across Borders
Jeannine Manuel School in London is proud to be part of a unique family of schools that includes École Jeannine Manuel in Paris and Lille. Together, we share a mission that guides each and every one of our decisions: to promote international understanding through the bilingual education of a multicultural community of students, and to foster pedagogical innovation by exploring best practices in an ever-changing global environment.
Our three schools are united by a commitment to pedagogical innovation, academic excellence, and a belief in the power of bilingualism to open minds and broaden perspectives.
Strength in Connection
Our close relationship with our sister schools fosters rich academic collaboration and alignment. We share teaching and learning practices, professional development resources, and a unified approach to bilingual and multicultural education that prepares students to succeed in any international context.
Ecole Jeannine Manuel, Paris
The Ecole Jeannine Manuel was originally founded in Paris in 1954. It now welcomes over 2,000 students representing more than 80 nationalities.
Ecole Jeannine Manuel, Lille
Founded in 1992, our boarding school, located a few miles from the metropolitan city of Lille, our Marcq-en-Baroeul campus welcomes more than 1000 students. The boarding school is home to 120 boarders that come from all corners of the globe, making it a truly international and multicultural community.

Extra-curricular
We believe that learning goes beyond the classroom and are proud to offer over 60 clubs for our students. Every day, we offer extracurricular activities for Early Years, Primary and Secondary School students. Whether your child loves coding or cooking, drama or debate, sport or science, there's something for everyone!
Our MUN club is one of the most popular, and for good reason - our students consistently do brilliantly at top international conferences. It’s a chance to debate real-world issues, meet peers from other schools, and use the oracy skills developed at school!
Our climbing wall is located right here at school, giving students the chance to climb during the week without heading off-site. It’s a great way to get moving, try something new, and build confidence in a safe and encouraging environment.
Our Ballet Club introduces our youngest students to movement, rhythm and creativity in a joyful and nurturing environment, helping them build confidence, coordination and a love of dance.
Our Chess Club encourages strategic thinking, concentration and problem-solving in a calm and engaging environment, welcoming students of all levels to learn and play together.
A fantastic way for students to challenge themselves, discover new interests, and grow as individuals, all while having fun with friends and making lasting memories. Find out more about our programme!
We have several student-run newspaper clubs across the school, where budding writers, editors and designers bring stories to life. Recently, a group of Middle School students had the chance to visit The Guardian offices - a behind-the-scenes look at professional journalism in action.
We are proud to have several Art Clubs to suit all ages, encouraging creativity, imagination and self-expression through a range of fun and inspiring artistic activities!
Making the most of our outdoor spaces, children plant, observe, and care for nature - learning to understand and appreciate the living world around them!
Improv is where quick thinking meets creativity in both French and English. Students build confidence as they play with language, sharpen their listening skills, and learn to express themselves clearly and spontaneously.
From hand-built bowls to sculpted creatures, this club invites students to get creative with clay. It’s a calm, tactile space where they can shape, decorate and experiment while building fine motor skills and artistic confidence along the way.
One of several sports clubs in Middle School, gymnastics helps students develop strength, flexibility and balance in a supportive and energetic setting!
From Python coding to Dungeons & Dragons, we are also proud to have many student-led clubs at school!
One of several STEM clubs in Primary, Cypher Coding gives students the chance to deepen their coding and computational thinking skills in a fun, hands-on environment. It’s a space to explore, solve problems, and think like a programmer!
Our Netball Club helps students build teamwork, confidence and resilience in a fun and supportive environment, while developing skills and a love of sport.
A fun way to help students develop discipline, confidence and resilience while improving strength, coordination and focus in a supportive and energetic environment!
Our Football Club gives students the opportunity to develop their skills, teamwork and confidence while enjoying the game. Alongside regular training sessions, Jeannine Manuel School has official football teams that compete against other schools!
We are proud to offer a selection of over 60 clubs! Contact us for more information.
Announcing our new Home Languages Programme
From September, our Home Language Programme will offer students already fluent in Arabic, Italian or Russian the opportunity to further develop and celebrate their linguistic and cultural heritage beyond the classroom. The programme will be available for students from Year 1 to Year 10. Delivered after school in age-appropriate groups, the programme is designed to nurture confidence, fluency, and a deeper connection to students’ home languages through engaging weekly sessions tailored to each stage of learning.
Request more information
Our clubs are a chance for students to try something new and enjoy time with others. From discovering hidden talents to building new skills, the experience is as enriching as it is enjoyable. With activities available every day in Early Years, Primary and Middle School, there are regular opportunities to explore new interests and build skills. Clubs run in both French and English and reflect the full range of our students’ passions. Our club offering changes twice yearly, so expect new clubs to be available regularly!
Want to find out more?
Contact our Admissions Office for the full extracurricular brochure

pageCache.text:
Early Years & Primary (Nursery - Year 6)
From their earliest years, pupils are immersed in a caring, bilingual environment where curiosity, confidence, and a love of learning take root. Throughout Primary, this journey deepens through an ambitious curriculum taught in French and English, enriched by Mandarin, a specialist Music Programme in the Early Years, and a broad academic programme. Outstanding facilities and expert teaching enable every child to thrive and grow. Discover our Early Years & Primary School!
Did you know?
In the Early Years and Primary School, we admit students with no knowledge of French and/or English and bring them to proficiency through our specialist French+ and/or English+ programmes.
